still_open.problem: The inserted alphabet and the draw alphabet both hold the single quote and the tab. Those two are refused only inside a span. A quote can close the span, and a tab is then a legal separator before a second quoted argument. Seeds 4050 and 19019 both draw vsdd survey --flag value 'x'<TAB>'', a correct plain call. The grammar and the parser accept it (args survey, --flag, value, x, ''), and sh, bash 3.2, bash 5.3, dash and zsh all run vsdd with those arguments. With the code unchanged, setting the seeds to (4050, 19019) fails the test. The precondition assertion holds for this text, so it does not stop it. The new comment that 'no draw can be a correct plain call whatever the seed' is false. The six seeds in the file pass only by luck; 2 of seeds 0 to 19999 draw such a text.
still_open.proposed_fix: Leave the tab (U+0009) out of both inside and refused. test_every_control_character_is_refused_between_quotes already pins the tab inside a span. With no space or tab in the alphabets, any quote closes the span right before a non-blank character, and every other refused character is refused anywhere, so every draw is refused. A scan of seeds 0 to 19999 then finds 0 approved draws. Make the precondition assertion match, and correct the comment.

still_open.problem: Five argument-position reverts fail none of the 77 tests. (1) Adding '$' to _SAFE: is_vsdd_call then approves vsdd survey $x. The '$' row also holds parentheses. (2) Adding '(' to _SAFE: the '(' row also holds ')'. Only the parser refuses vsdd survey a(b. (3) Dropping (?!=) from the quoted prefix: is_vsdd_call then approves vsdd survey ='hid', and zsh -f turns ='a' into the path of the command a. (4) Letting CR into the separator: is_vsdd_call then approves vsdd survey<CR>hid. (5) Letting LF into the separator, or CR into the leading blanks: these are refused only by the parser. The current code refuses all of these. The gap predates this round.
